_doc: Stream E (play-test 5, T25 ANGLING) — the TEXT content of angling: what there is to catch, cook, buy and who teaches it. The numbers of the loop (bite wait, tug difficulty, skill gain, table weights by rarity) are stream C's (js/rules/fishing.js + data/rules/fishing.json); pool positions are data/provinces/angling-pools.json; the quests are data/quests/angling.json. `fish[]`: id, name, desc, water (river | lake | marsh | coast — marsh = fresh water in a marsh/fen biome), bands [lo, hi] = the zone LEVELS it lives in (a zone offers a fish when the zone's band overlaps), time (any | day | night | dawn | dusk), rarity (common | uncommon | rare | epic), size [minCm, maxCm], price (gold a merchant pays), skill (angling skill needed), pool: true = only from a fish pool. `junk[]`: worthless catches. `legends[]`: one named fish per zone (zone = sheet zone id): landing it gives the `trophy` item and the `title` ('<name> <title>'). `pullBack[]`: 'something pulls back' — a monster `type` (Farhold bestiary id) climbs out, by water kind and zone band. `crates`: the chance of a sunken crate and the T9 crate it is. `meals{}`: same shape as data/provinces/shops.json goodsCatalog (the existing food + buff code eats them). `recipes[]`: cooked at a campfire or inn hearth; needs = [{fish: id, count}] or [{tag: any | river | lake | marsh | coast | <rarity>, count}]; skill = angling skill needed to know it. `tools[]`: rods (a Tool item, no weapon slot; bonus.band = wider tug band, bonus.wait = shorter bite wait). `bait[]`: optional consumables. `anglers[]`: one per town; they sell `sells`, buy fish and give angler jobs (data/quests/jobs.json frames with a `fish` slot). `skill.ranks`: rank name from each skill value up. OWNER FEEDBACK 7 (V2): `price` is a species' worth RELATIVE to other fish, deliberately spread wide — common 1-4, uncommon 6-14, rare 30-60, epic 150-300 — and a legend carries its own `price` (500 + 20 x its skill). Stream C's fishing.json `value` turns it into gold (rarity factor x mult x the zone-level factor); tools/sim-economy.mjs measures the hour.

fish.name: Silver Perch
fish.desc: Bites at anything shiny, including its own reflection.

fish.name: Mudlip Gudgeon
fish.desc: A small brown opinion on the state of the riverbed.

fish.name: Ford Dace
fish.desc: Lives where carts cross and has seen every wheel in the province.

fish.name: Millrace Chub
fish.desc: Fat from stolen grain. The miller wants a word.

fish.name: Redfin Roach
fish.desc: Common as mud and twice as easy to cook.

fish.name: Tollbridge Pike
fish.desc: Waits under bridges and charges whatever it can swallow.

fish.name: Dawn Grayling
fish.desc: Rises with the mist and is gone by breakfast.

fish.name: Copper Barbel
fish.desc: Whiskered, heavy and stubborn. Pulls like a debt.

fish.name: Lantern Eel
fish.desc: Glows faintly. Tastes of nothing you can prove.

fish.name: Brook Speckle
fish.desc: A small trout with a great many freckles and no patience.

fish.name: Weir Salmon
fish.desc: Has jumped every weir in Torbor Downs and resents all of them.

fish.name: Pilgrim Trout
fish.desc: Swims upstream to Saint Orrin's every year. Nobody knows what it prays for.

fish.name: Reeve's Sturgeon
fish.desc: By old law it belongs to the reeve. By older law, to whoever lands it.

fish.name: Pond Bream
fish.desc: Flat, calm and entirely without ambition.

fish.name: Greenback Carp
fish.desc: Older than most hamlets and not shy about it.

fish.name: Reed Rudd
fish.desc: Hides in the reeds. Badly.

fish.name: Stone Loach
fish.desc: Looks like a pebble. Fights like one too.

fish.name: Moon Tench
fish.desc: Slick, green and only awake when you would rather not be.

fish.name: Gullwick Whitefish
fish.desc: The lakes' daily bread. The gulls agree.

fish.name: Glass Minnow
fish.desc: You can see its lunch. It can see yours.

fish.name: Mere Zander
fish.desc: All teeth and bad temper, wrapped in a nice fillet.

fish.name: Deepwater Char
fish.desc: Comes up from the cold dark for one reason: your bait.

fish.name: Pale Carp
fish.desc: White as a sheet. The monks say it is a sign. They say that about everything.

fish.name: Coldwater Lamprey
fish.desc: Not a fish you catch so much as one you detach.

fish.name: Crowned Pike
fish.desc: Wears a ridge of bony knobs and rules its bay like a bad baron.

fish.name: Bog Bullhead
fish.desc: All head. The rest is an afterthought.

fish.name: Fen Stickleback
fish.desc: Three spines and a grudge.

fish.name: Mire Mudskipper
fish.desc: Technically a fish. It has heard the arguments.

fish.name: Black Weatherfish
fish.desc: Wriggles before rain. Wriggles after rain. A poor forecaster.

fish.name: Brackwater Eel
fish.desc: The fen's main export, after damp.

fish.name: Wisp Gar
fish.desc: Follows marsh lights around at night. Nobody has asked why.

fish.name: Sedge Snakehead
fish.desc: Breathes air, crosses fields and has opinions about ducks.

fish.name: Peat Catfish
fish.desc: Brown water, brown fish, brown stew. Delicious.

fish.name: Sunkenlight Angler
fish.desc: Carries its own lamp, which is more than most fen travellers do.

fish.name: Greywhisker Wels
fish.desc: A catfish the size of a calf. Something has been feeding it.

fish.name: Oldmud Lungfish
fish.desc: Sleeps through droughts and wakes up angry. Has seen four of them.

fish.name: Harbour Sprat
fish.desc: Comes by the thousand. You will catch one.

fish.name: Sand Dab
fish.desc: Flat on purpose.

fish.name: Saltmouth Herring
fish.desc: Smoked, salted, pickled or fresh. The town does little else.

fish.name: Tide Mullet
fish.desc: Arrives with the tide and leaves with your bait.

fish.name: Rock Wrasse
fish.desc: Bright as a painted door and about as easy to get out of the rocks.

fish.name: Grey Gurnard
fish.desc: Grunts when landed. So would you.

fish.name: Wreckers' Conger
fish.desc: Lives in sunk hulls and guards cargo it has no use for.

fish.name: Storm Bass
fish.desc: Feeds in the surf when sensible people are indoors.

fish.name: Moonscale Ray
fish.desc: Glides in on bright nights. Handle from the polite end.

fish.name: Longbill Spearfish
fish.desc: Every captain in Saltmouth has nearly caught one. Ask them. At length.

fish.name: Foldside Tench
fish.desc: Fat, slow and fond of the sheep-wash. The first fish most Torbor children land.

fish.name: Sheepwash Trout
fish.desc: Lies under the fold bridge and judges every bait on its merits.

fish.name: Sedge Pickerel
fish.desc: A pike in miniature with a pike's opinion of itself.

fish.name: Quay Whiting
fish.desc: Shoals under the fish stalls, living on what the gulls drop.

fish.name: Torbor Goldscale
fish.desc: Every scale a new coin. Innkeepers pay for it before it is cooked, so it can be seen on the plate.

fish.name: Highforce Trout
fish.desc: Holds station under the falls and takes whatever the white water brings.

fish.name: Ironback Barbel
fish.desc: Plated like a gauntlet and about as easy to turn.

fish.name: Kingsrun Salmon
fish.desc: Runs the high rivers once a year and was once reserved for one table.

fish.name: Tarn Whitefish
fish.desc: Pale as the snowmelt it lives in, and nearly as cold to hold.

fish.name: Deepmere Pike
fish.desc: Old enough to have outlived the boat that first hooked it.

fish.name: Starless Char
fish.desc: Black above, black below; anglers find it by the hole it leaves in the reflections.

fish.name: Blackwater Bowfin
fish.desc: Breathes air when the bog runs out of anything better.

fish.name: Fenlord Catfish
fish.desc: Rules a mile of drowned ditch and takes tribute in ducklings.

fish.name: Shoal Mackerel
fish.desc: Comes in thousands or not at all.

fish.name: Greatfin Tunny
fish.desc: Fast enough to be somewhere else before the float settles.

fish.name: Abyss Halibut
fish.desc: A flat acre of muscle from where the charts stop. Both eyes are on you.

junk.name: Old Boot
junk.desc: Left foot. The right one is still out there.

junk.name: Waterlogged Hat
junk.desc: Somebody was having a worse day than you.

junk.name: Bent Horseshoe
junk.desc: Unlucky for the horse, mildly lucky for you.

junk.name: Rusty Bucket
junk.desc: Holds almost no water, which is how it ended up down there.

junk.name: Cart Wheel Spoke
junk.desc: The Carter would like it back. The Carter can whistle.

junk.name: Soggy Ledger
junk.desc: Every page reads the same now: blue.

junk.name: Cracked Jug
junk.desc: Still smells of trail ale. So does the fish that lived in it.

junk.name: Somebody's Lost Bobber
junk.desc: Painted with care, lost with swearing.

junk.name: Bent Toll Token
junk.desc: Good for one crossing of a bridge that fell down years ago.

junk.name: Chewed Oar Blade
junk.desc: Tooth marks the width of your hand. Best not to think about it.

legends.name: Old Ploughshare
legends.desc: A carp as long as a harrow, seen in the Torbor every spring since the bridge was wood.
legends.title: the Patient

trophy.name: Old Ploughshare's Scale
trophy.desc: A scale the size of a saucer. It still smells of the Torbor.

legends.name: The Penitent
legends.desc: A white trout that circles the pilgrims' ford and has never once taken a blessed bait.
legends.title: the Unblessed

trophy.name: The Penitent's Fin
trophy.desc: Pale as candle wax. The Prior asked you not to hang it in the yard.

legends.name: Copperjaw
legends.desc: A barbel that has swallowed so many miners' hooks its mouth has gone green.
legends.title: Hook-Taker

trophy.name: Copperjaw's Hoard
trophy.desc: Thirty-one hooks, two lures and a spoon, all from one fish.

legends.name: Mossback
legends.desc: A pike so old that things grow on it. Some of the things have names.
legends.title: of the Deep Wood

trophy.name: Mossback's Jaw
trophy.desc: More teeth than a fish needs and a small fern.

legends.name: The Miller's Debt
legends.desc: The chub that broke three wheels at Millbrook. The miller keeps a list.
legends.title: Wheelbreaker

trophy.name: The Miller's Receipt
trophy.desc: A signed note: "Paid in full. One fish."

legends.name: The Tollkeeper
legends.desc: A pike under Halsbridge that takes one duck a day and considers it fair.
legends.title: the Bridge-Warden

trophy.name: The Tollkeeper's Tooth
trophy.desc: Long as a finger. The ducks sent their thanks.

legends.name: The Cistern Pale
legends.desc: A blind white eel from the flooded cellars of Ashcombe. It finds you by the sound of your heart.
legends.title: Cellar-Fisher

trophy.name: A Blind Eel's Lamp
trophy.desc: It never had eyes. This is the old lantern it lived in.

legends.name: Snowmelt
legends.desc: A char that comes down with the thaw, cold enough to numb the hand that lifts it.
legends.title: the Frostbitten

trophy.name: Snowmelt's Ice
trophy.desc: A lump of ice from its belly that has not melted yet.

legends.name: Grandfather Mud
legends.desc: A lungfish older than Brackwater. The fen folk leave it bread and do not say why.
legends.title: Fen-Friend

trophy.name: Grandfather's Whisker
trophy.desc: As long as your arm and still twitching a little.

legends.name: The Fifth Lake
legends.desc: There are four Gullwick lakes. The fishers say the fifth one swims.
legends.title: Lake-Lander

trophy.name: Chart of the Fifth Lake
trophy.desc: A fisher's chart with one lake drawn in and crossed out, many times.

legends.name: Bellmouth
legends.desc: A zander that swallowed the Coldwater chapel bell. On still nights it tolls.
legends.title: the Bell-Ringer

trophy.name: The Coldwater Clapper
trophy.desc: The clapper of a small bell, polished by years of stomach.

legends.name: The Harbourmaster
legends.desc: A conger that has sunk two skiffs and inspects every hull that comes in.
legends.title: Skiff-Saver

trophy.name: The Harbourmaster's Seal
trophy.desc: A brass harbour seal it had no business owning.

legends.name: The Red Runner
legends.desc: A salmon stained by the cliff clay. It has outrun every net on the frontier.
legends.title: the Outrunner

trophy.name: Red Runner's Tail
trophy.desc: Still stained red. The colour does not wash out.

legends.name: Deserter's Supper
legends.desc: A barbel grown fat on rations thrown in the river by men leaving in a hurry.
legends.title: Ration-Thief

trophy.name: A Full Mess Tin
trophy.desc: Recovered from the fish, lid on, contents best left alone.

legends.name: Thornbelly
legends.desc: Something the blight got into. The Scar has no water left, so it went downhill to the Coldwater meres, and it is not sorry.
legends.title: the Unspoiled

trophy.name: Thornbelly's Spine
trophy.desc: A ridge of black thorns. Do not hang it over the bed.

legends.name: Steeplejack
legends.desc: A sturgeon that lives in the nave of a drowned church and is exactly as long as its aisle.
legends.title: of the Sunken Wolds

trophy.name: Steeplejack's Plate
trophy.desc: One armour plate from its back. It makes a decent buckler.

pullBack.say: Something pulls back. It is coming up the bank.
The line goes slack, then the water stands up.
Your catch has legs, a temper and friends.
You have hooked the pond itself.
Your catch has legs, a temper and friends.
The line goes slack, then the surf stands up.
Something pulls back. It is coming up the beach.

crates.say: The hook snags on something square. A sunken crate!

charred_fish_on_a_stick.name: Fish on a Stick
charred_fish_on_a_stick.desc: Any fish, any stick, any fire. Eat out of combat to recover health over 20 seconds.

fried_perch.name: Pan-Fried Perch
fried_perch.desc: Crisp skin, a few bones. Eat out of combat: recover health over 20 seconds, then +3% health for 30 minutes.

river_chowder.name: Riverbank Chowder
river_chowder.desc: Three kinds of fish and a potato that floated past. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +5% health for 30 minutes.

smoked_eel.name: Smoked Eel
smoked_eel.desc: Chewy, smoky and stays with you. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +4% armour for 30 minutes.

pike_steaks.name: Pike Steaks
pike_steaks.desc: Mostly bone, and the rest makes up for it. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +3% damage for 30 minutes.

fen_stew.name: Brown Fen Stew
fen_stew.desc: Do not ask what is in it. It is fish. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +6% health for 30 minutes.

herring_pie.name: Saltmouth Herring Pie
herring_pie.desc: The heads look out of the crust. They are not judging you. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +5% armour for 45 minutes.

archers_fishcakes.name: Archer's Fishcakes
archers_fishcakes.desc: Light enough to shoot straight after. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +4% ranged damage for 30 minutes.

pilgrims_supper.name: Pilgrim's Supper
pilgrims_supper.desc: Trout baked in a blessing and a lot of butter. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +6% damage to the undead for 30 minutes.

anglers_feast.name: Angler's Feast
anglers_feast.desc: A rare fish done properly. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +4% damage for 60 minutes.

legends_broth.name: Broth of the One That Did Not Get Away
legends_broth.desc: Made from a fish people will not believe you caught. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +8% health for 60 minutes.

riders_kedgeree.name: Rider's Kedgeree
riders_kedgeree.desc: Eaten in the saddle by people in a hurry. Recover health over 20 seconds, then +10% mount speed for 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Fish on a Stick
recipes.desc: Hold it over the fire until it stops looking at you.

recipes.name: Riverbank Chowder
recipes.desc: Three river fish, whatever they are.

recipes.name: Smoked Eel
recipes.desc: Hang an eel in the smoke and find something else to do.

recipes.name: Pike Steaks
recipes.desc: One pike feeds a party, if the party is patient with bones.

recipes.name: Brown Fen Stew
recipes.desc: Three marsh fish, boiled until brown.

recipes.name: Archer's Fishcakes
recipes.desc: Two lake fish, mashed and fried.

recipes.name: Pilgrim's Supper
recipes.desc: One Pilgrim Trout. It would have wanted this. Probably.

recipes.name: Rider's Kedgeree
recipes.desc: Two coast fish and yesterday's rations.

recipes.name: Angler's Feast
recipes.desc: Any rare fish, and the good pan.

recipes.name: Broth of the One That Did Not Get Away
recipes.desc: Any epic fish. Do not rush it.

tools.name: Hazel Rod
tools.desc: A hazel switch, a length of line and a hook. A Tool: it takes no weapon slot. Lets you fish any water.

tools.name: Whippy Ash Rod
tools.desc: Longer, springier and far too good for gudgeon. The tug band is 15% wider.

tools.name: River Warden's Rod
tools.desc: Split cane with a brass reel. The tug band is 25% wider and bites come 20% sooner.

bait.name: Tin of Worms
bait.desc: Ten worms. Bites come 25% sooner for the next ten casts.

bait.name: Bread Paste
bait.desc: Common fish cannot resist it; rare fish can. Ten casts with fewer junk catches.

bait.name: Bright Tin Lure
bait.desc: Flashes like a perch's dream. Ten casts with a better chance at uncommon and rare fish.

anglers.name: Tam Sedgeley
anglers.greeting: Ever held a rod? No? Good. No bad habits to fix.

anglers.name: Sister Brindle
anglers.greeting: The Prior calls it idleness. I call it contemplation with a hook in it.

anglers.name: Dunmer Slagfoot
anglers.greeting: Twelve hours underground, then I come up here and stare at water. Do not talk to me about ore.

anglers.name: Old Nettie Cray
anglers.greeting: The cellars flooded forty years back. The fishing has never been better.

anglers.name: Perrin Underarch
anglers.greeting: Best spot in the province is right under the bridge. The pike thinks so too.

anglers.name: Quiet Oswin
anglers.greeting: ...Shh. You will scare them. Fine. What do you want?

anglers.name: Greta Icewell
anglers.greeting: Cut a hole, drop a line, do not fall in. That is the whole craft up here.

anglers.name: Mog Eelwright
anglers.greeting: If it wriggles, I sell it. If it does not, give it a minute.

anglers.name: Skipper Hale Tarrow
anglers.greeting: Rivers! Ponds! Hah. Come back when you have been pulled off a harbour wall.

anglers.name: Josey Fourlakes
anglers.greeting: Four lakes, and I have a favourite stone on each. No, I will not say which.

anglers.name: Corwen Claywater
anglers.greeting: The river runs red here. It is only the clay. Mostly it is the clay.

anglers.name: Wick Thornaby
anglers.greeting: Throw back anything with thorns. Throw back anything that asks you to.

anglers.name: Jed Weirside
anglers.greeting: The miller says the chub are his. The chub and I disagree.

anglers.name: Marta Stillmere
anglers.greeting: Hear that bell? There is no bell. Lovely evening for it, though.

anglers.name: Corporal Finch Loach
anglers.greeting: Sentry duty by the river, they said. Nobody said I could not bring a rod.

anglers.name: Ysmay Drownfield
anglers.greeting: My grandmother's house is under that water. The perch keep it tidy.
